Subject: Triage notes: Stonebridge on-prem spike — initial hypotheses

Summary of initial triage (logs + attached counters):
- Pattern: short-lived bursts where tokenization stage stalls for ~600-1200ms, followed by decoder retries and 502/503 surface.
- Hardware signals: sustained NVLINK queue depth growth concurrent with elevated PCIe recovers on GPU nodes 3-5. GPUs report nominal utilization, but peer-to-peer transfers are queuing.
- Runtime observations: per-request batch size variance increased (client-side jitter), leading to frequent kernel selection thrash in our JIT path. This increases micro-scheduling and causes NVLINK pressure under our default multi-NUMA concurrency.

Immediate mitigations we can push (no downtime):
1) Force single-NUMA thread affinity for runtime (reduces cross-NUMA nvlink pressure).
2) Turn off aggressive JIT batch fusion for affected model (runtime knob) — falls back to stable kernel path.
3) Temporarily cap concurrency per GPU from 12 -> 6 and enable conservative batching window.

Risks: latency p50 may rise slightly for small single-request flows; p99 should recover. We recommend a controlled canary (10% of traffic) for 30 minutes before account-wide rollout.

Action items:
- Jonas: schedule 15m canary call with Stonebridge (Emily + Marcus) for 10:30 PT.
- Marissa: prepare a concise customer-facing note (what we will change, monitoring plan, rollback).
- Vivek: prepare config diff and a hotpatch script.
- I'll open SUP-6789 and attach runbook.

Subject: Mitigation applied & monitoring update — SUP-6789

Status update (post-canary):
- Implemented mitigations at 10:38 PT on 23-Nov to 10% canary traffic: single-NUMA affinity + cap concurrency to 6 + JIT fusion disabled for the model.
- Immediate effect: p99 dropped from >2s to ~260ms in the canary cohort within 8 minutes. Error rate in canary fell from 3.8% -> 0.2%.
- Account-wide rollout started at 11:05 PT; completed by 11:22 PT. Post-rollout aggregate p99 stabilized at ~240-300ms, error rate <0.5%.
- Root cause hypothesis refined: client-side batch jitter + JIT kernel selection thrash caused micro-bursts of NVLINK contention on multi-NUMA node configs. Reproducible under skewed request-size distributions.

Next steps:
1) Short term (this week): push recommended runtime patch to include conservative kernel-fallback heuristics and publish client-side batching guidance to Stonebridge.
2) Mid term (2-4 weeks): testing for improved kernel-selection stability under request-size variance and a telemetry signal to auto-constrain concurrency when nvlink queue depth rises.
3) Commercial: Marissa to coordinate exec note and proposed credit options (Jonas/Rishi to own).
